channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Former national director to chair trust
item.description: A former Health Education England medical director has been appointed to chair a specialist acute trust.

item.title: Speak Up Guardian claims she was silenced by top trust’s leaders
item.description: An “outstanding”-rated trust is contesting an unfair dismissal claim from its former Freedom to Speak Up Guardian, who claims she was punished for raising concerns with senior leaders.

item.title: Winners of the 2026 HSJ Awards revealed
item.description: The winners of the 2026 HSJ Awards were announced last night.

item.title: Consultancy wins £41m single patient record contract
item.description: NHS England has awarded a £41m contract to a big four consultancy firm to support a range of major technology initiatives.

item.title: Revealed: The trust where 40% of A&E patients end up in a corridor
item.description: The number of patients in corridors represents around a quarter of A&E attendances at some trusts – with the ratio rising to nearly 40 per cent at one major teaching hospital – figures suggest.

item.title: ‘Overly complex’ £22m procurement ‘must be abandoned’
item.description: A trust has been told to abandon an “overly complex” £22m procurement for renal services after being found to have breached 16 Provider Selection Regime regulations.

item.title: Trust ‘faces £3m payout’ after whistleblower ruling
item.description: A teaching hospital trust could face a potential £3m payout to a whistleblower who accused “senior people” at the trust of concealing information relating to deaths, patient mistreatment and sexual assaults, after a tribunal threw out its defence to her unfair dismissal case.

item.title: Revealed: One in five pensions paid late
item.description: There were so many delays to NHS pensions over the past 18 months that government had to pay out millions in compensation for lost interest.

item.title: Cooper vows to ‘refocus’ neighbourhood health reform
item.description: The health and social care secretary has pledged to “refocus” neighbourhood health reforms away from “boundaries [and] restructuring”.

item.title: ‘Senior people’ accused of covering up death and sexual assault allegations
item.description: A former head of safeguarding has accused “senior people” at a teaching hospital of concealing information relating to deaths, mistreatment of patients and sexual assaults, a tribunal heard.

item.title: Milburn wants new waiting time target by 2028
item.description: National maximum waiting times for children and young people’s mental health services should be in place by 2028, according to an influential government report.

item.title: ICBs join forces to cut hospital activity
item.description: Integrated care board leaders have agreed five national metrics that will be used to judge their success, mostly focused on curbing hospital activity, MPs have been told.

item.title: Government extends controversial tech contract for two years
item.description: The government has extended Palantir’s contract to run the federated data platform for another two years.

item.title: Revealed: Hospitals stuck for years in ‘ineffective’ NHSE maternity scheme
item.description: Six trusts have spent more than four years in NHS England’s maternity improvement programme, which experts and families now say is “not fit for purpose”.

item.title: Ex-NHS chief hired as mayor’s health lead
item.description: A mayoral authority has appointed a former commissioning boss as its health lead.

item.title: Chief inspector quits just one year into role
item.description: The Care Quality Commission’s chief inspector of hospitals is leaving unexpectedly after just one year in the job to become an NHS regional medical director, it has emerged.

item.title: Chair swaps community trust for acute neighbour
item.description: The chair of a community trust is leaving to take up the same role at an adjoining acute trust.

item.title: Revealed: £2.8bn delayed discharges cost soars past projection
item.description: Delayed discharges have cost the NHS an estimated £2.8bn in the past 12 months – significantly higher than a projection made this time last year based on NHS England’s data.

item.title: CEO joins trust from special measures health board
item.description: The chief executive of the largest health board in Wales – which has been in special measures for three years – is set to lead a trust in the North West.

item.title: Trust and ICB deficit £200m worse than last year
item.description: Trusts and integrated care boards were £210m further behind plan halfway through this financial year than a year earlier, and the net deficit is a fifth larger.
